name: Westrock Coffee - Conway AR Roast-to-RTD Plant

fieldNotes.location: Confirmed as the former Kimberly-Clark Conway paper-products plant at 480 Exchange Avenue, now Westrock Coffee's roast-to-RTD facility ($315M, 570K sq ft, ~45 acres, opened June 2024). The roster pin sat at the NE construction/laydown corner; locked center moved SW to the main building mass at 35.0721,-92.4188.
fieldNotes.truckGate: A sliding chain-link gate across a truck driveway is clearly visible in 2024-08 Street View on the NE side of the property (near 35.0760,-92.4188), with continuous chain-link perimeter fencing running along the warehouse face. The truck/yard side of the campus is access-controlled.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed guard booth was positively identified at the truck gate in available imagery. The NE truck gate is a rolling chain-link gate with no adjacent booth visible — implying remote/kiosk check-in. A large former-paper-mill campus of this scale may have a manned gate elsewhere; marked uncertain.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: Truck gate present, no guard shack seen — remote check-in inferred.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Large dedicated trailer drop yard on the NE flank of the plant (wc-rtd-dropyard-z19) holding ~60-85 trailers parked in rows, separate from active dock staging.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Drop yard rows visibly hold well over 50 trailers — banded 50+.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Dock doors distributed across multiple building faces (NE drop-yard side and the SE face along I-40). ~30-45 doors estimated across the sprawling complex; exact count limited by roof complexity and scale — banded 25-50.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus-scale site: a sprawling main manufacturing building plus several distinct ancillary/warehouse structures (NE warehouse, NW building, support buildings) within one fenced property.
fieldNotes.railServed: A rail line runs along the south edge of the property (visible in wc-rtd-sw); former Kimberly-Clark paper mills were rail-served and a spur appears to enter the site.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Very wide paved aprons and multiple driveways/access points give ample room to add an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Inside the Conway industrial fabric directly along Interstate I-40 with dense surrounding commercial/retail development — judged Urban.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Extensive paved internal yard provides holding/queue room inside the fence before the docks.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: The internal gate-to-dock approach is long and can stack 3+ trucks.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale positively identified; marked uncertain given site scale.
